inline_comments.comment:
The root node is positioned at `rootY + 20` — a bare magic number with no comment explaining its purpose. Extract it to a named constant:

```typescript
const ROOT_NODE_Y_OFFSET = 20; // visual centering offset
...
y: rootY + ROOT_NODE_Y_OFFSET,
```

`_drawNodes` and `_updateNodeDimensions` (which uses the `FilledMindMapNode` type imported at line 8) are both defined but never called anywhere in the new renderer — the `draw` function goes directly through `db.getData()` → `render(data4Layout, svg)`. These are dead code along with the `drawNode` import from `'./svgDraw.js'` and the `FilledMindMapNode` type import. Remove all four to avoid misleading future readers.

The hardcoded dimensions `height = 46` and `width = 92` for `rect`-shape mindmap nodes are magic numbers with no explanation, and they bypass the actual bounding-box calculation that happens inside `insertNode`. These should come from a named constant in `defaultConfig.mindmap` or be removed so the renderer relies on the shape's own measurement.

Also, `cloud`, `bang`, and `defaultMindmapNode` shapes do not receive `node.from = 'mindmap'`, which means the `from`-gated paths in `drawRect`, `roundedRect`, and `circle` will not trigger for these shapes — verify this is intentional.

`nodeType.DEFAULT` and `nodeType.NO_BORDER` are both defined as `0`, so the switch statement in `getShapeFromType` can only match one case for value `0`. The `case nodeType.NO_BORDER:` branch (if it existed) would be unreachable. As written, ALL type-0 nodes — including those intended to have no border — will map to `'defaultMindmapNode'` instead of `'rect'`. Verify whether `NO_BORDER` is supposed to render identically to `DEFAULT`, or assign distinct numeric values.

`diagramId: 'mindmap-' + Date.now()` is immediately overwritten by `data4Layout.diagramId = id` in the renderer, so the `Date.now()` call is dead code. Remove it and either leave `diagramId` unset or assign a deterministic placeholder:

```typescript
diagramId: 'mindmap',  // will be overridden by the renderer
```

Similarly, `nodeSpacing`, `rankSpacing`, and `shapes` added to the returned object are not consumed by any registered layout algorithm. Remove them or document the intended consumer.

Changing `isGroup: boolean` to `isGroup?: boolean` in `BaseNode` is a breaking change for any code that previously narrowed on this field without an `undefined` guard. While `ClusterNode` and `NonClusterNode` still redeclare it as required (`true` / `false` respectively), code typed as `BaseNode` (not `Node`) now sees an optional field. Per project rules, fields should not be marked optional if they are unconditionally initialized — and both concrete subtypes always set it. Revert to required in `BaseNode`.

The `Edge` interface now contains both `start`/`end` (existing fields) and the new `source`/`target` fields, which appear to represent the same relationship. This duplication is confusing and will require callers to keep both pairs in sync. Either alias one set to the other, or document exactly which fields each layout renderer is expected to use.

Using `node.from === 'mindmap'` as a runtime discriminator inside the generic `drawRect` (and also in `squareRect.ts` and `roundedRect.ts`, as well as `circle.ts`) couples the generic shape renderer to mindmap-specific layout decisions. This is the same concern in all four files.

The clean solution is to express the mindmap-specific padding/sizing through already-existing node properties (`node.padding`, `node.radius`, `node.taper`) — set those values in the mindmap renderer before calling `insertNode`, and remove the `from` branches from the shape files entirely. This keeps shape renderers diagram-agnostic.

The edge-processing section is saturated with development-marker log calls (`'APA01 ...'`, `JSON.stringify(elkGraph, null, 2)`) that must not reach production. Stringifying the full ELK graph on every render is a significant performance regression for large diagrams. Per project conventions, debugging output should use `log.debug` or `log.trace` with no numbered prefixes, and full-object serialisation should be removed. Please strip all `APA01`-prefixed log statements before merging.

`validateLayoutData` throws `'Root node is required'` if `data.rootNode` is absent. This makes a **generic** layout algorithm require a mindmap-specific field. Any other diagram type that registers cose-bilkent as its layout will immediately fail validation. Move the `rootNode` check into the mindmap-specific calling code (e.g. in the mindmap renderer before calling the layout), or remove it from the shared validator entirely.

The `types` field points to `dist/layouts.d.ts`, but the package's public entry point (`dist/mermaid-layout-tidy-tree.core.mjs`) is generated from `src/index.ts`, which re-exports from `layouts.ts` and also exports `render` and everything from `types.ts`. The `types` entry should point to `dist/index.d.ts` so that TypeScript consumers receive the full public API, not just `tidyTreeLayout`.

Also, `scripts` is an empty object — without build scripts, the package cannot be built as part of the monorepo. Add the missing `build` / `dev` scripts matching the pattern used by `mermaid-layout-elk`.

The module declaration types the default export as `any`, which removes all type-checking for cose-bilkent usage. The project already ships proper Cytoscape extension typings for fcose (`@types/cytoscape-fcose`). Consider contributing a similarly shaped `.d.ts` that at least types `coseBilkent` as `(cytoscape: cytoscape.Core) => void` to match the cytoscape plugin contract.

The new test file uses a `.js` extension while the existing mindmap test (`mindmap.spec.ts`) and all other rendering specs in the same directory use `.ts`. Per project convention, new test files must use the `.ts` extension for consistency and to catch type errors statically.

The installation instruction shows `npm install non-layered-tidy-tree-layout`, which is the underlying library, not the mermaid integration package. End users should install `@mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree`. Also, the feature description lacks the `(v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)` placeholder required by the docs pipeline to stamp the correct release version. Add both corrections:

```markdown
## Tidy Tree Layouts (v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)
...
```sh
npm install @mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree
```
```

general_comments.comment: **`from: 'mindmap'` pattern across generic shape renderers.** Four generic shape files (`drawRect.ts`, `squareRect.ts`, `roundedRect.ts`, `circle.ts`) now branch on `node.from === 'mindmap'` to apply mindmap-specific sizing and padding. This is a significant design smell: the shape rendering layer must not know which diagram type is using it. The correct approach is to set the desired sizing properties (`node.padding`, `node.radius`, `node.taper`, etc.) in the mindmap renderer before calling `insertNode`, and let the shapes use those values uniformly. The `from` discriminator should be removed from all shape files.

**`_drawNodes`, `_updateNodeDimensions`, and their imports are dead code.** After the mindmap renderer was migrated to the unified rendering pipeline, the old node-drawing helpers were left in the file with underscore-prefixed names but are never invoked. The import of `drawNode` from `'./svgDraw.js'` and `FilledMindMapNode` from `'./mindmapTypes.js'` are also unused as a result. All four should be removed to prevent the file from growing misleadingly complex.

**`getData()` emits several unused fields.** The `MindmapDB.getData()` method returns `nodeSpacing`, `rankSpacing`, and `shapes` (as a plain object built from a `Map`) that are not consumed by the ELK, dagre, or cose-bilkent layout renderers. Unused data in the layout payload increases memory use and creates maintenance confusion about what the contract of `LayoutData` actually is. Either document the consumer for each extra field, or remove the fields until a concrete consumer exists.

**ELK renderer: full graph JSON stringification on every render.** The newly added debug statements include `JSON.stringify(elkGraph, null, 2)`, which serialises the entire ELK graph object — potentially with thousands of nodes and edges — on every render pass, even in production. In addition to the performance cost, this will print enormous log output at `debug` level. These statements must be removed (not just lowered to `trace`) before this is merged.

**Documentation examples should use ` ```mermaid-example ` fenced blocks.** The new layout examples in both `packages/mermaid/src/docs/config/tidy-tree.md` and the `Layouts` section added to `packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/mindmap.md` use plain ` ``` ` fences. The VitePress docs pipeline generates both the interactive editor and the rendered preview from ` ```mermaid-example ` blocks; plain fences will appear as raw code with no live preview on the published site.
